newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Man pleads insanity for New Zealand massacre.
newsitem.headline: Man pleads insanity for New Zealand massacre.

text.p: The man accused of one of New Zealand's most horrific mass murders pleaded not guilty on grounds of insanity in the High Court at Hamilton on Tuesday.
Six people were slain and six others wounded when a man wielding a shotgun cut a swathe through the small central North Island hamlet of Raurimu on February 8 this year.
Stephen Lawrence Anderson, 24, faces six charges of murder and eight of attempted murder.
Anderson stood quietly in the dock, flanked by two prison officers and a police officer. In a steady voice he emphasised the word "not" as he repeated "not guilty" to each charge.
Anderson's lawyer Stuart Grieve told the court his client's pleas would be based on a defence of insanity.
The shooting rampage began in the Anderson family's ski lodge in the Raurimu settlement, nestled in rolling hills beneath the majestic volcano Mount Ruapehu.
Witnesses said family and friends had gathered for breakfast on the first day of a holiday weekend when Anderson appeared at the door, levelled a gun at his father Neville, and shot him point blank.

Pandemonium broke out as the gunman began his shooting spree, killing and wounding several people in and around the lodge before proceeding onto another property, where a local resident was killed. The gunman then fled into the bush.
Anderson was arrested stark naked several hours after the shootings and has been in custody at a psychiatric hospital since.

The murders rocked New Zealand, which has prided itself on its peaceful image. The massacre, however, was the fifth mass slaughter in the country since 1990. Raurimu also sparked calls for a review of New Zealand's relatively liberal gun laws and put under fresh scrutiny its mental health system which mainly seeks to help patients while they remain in the community.
Anderson was diagnosed as paranoid schizophrenic last year and health authorities confirmed he had been a mental health patient.
Anderson was remanded in custody back to Tokanui Hospital.
Justice Penlington said Anderson's trial would start on December 1 and run for two weeks.
